questions.question: Who gave the concept of 'money illusion' for the first time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Irving Fisher.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Irving Fisher** gave the concept of **'money illusion'** for the first time.
 
• Money illusion refers to the tendency of people to think in** nominal terms** rather than real terms.
 
• For example, if a person's salary increases by** 3% but inflation is also 3%**, they may think they have received a raise when in reality their purchasing power has not changed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adam Smith** is known for his work on **economics.**

 
 
• He is often referred to as the** father of modern economics. **
 
 
 
• **JM Keynes **was a **renowned economist**.
 
 
• He is known for his theories on **macroeconomics **and the role of government in managing the economy.
 
 
 
• **Robertson** was an economist who contributed to the development of** monetary theory.**

questions.question: What is the rationale behind why one is ready to hold a ten rupee coin?

options.text: It is finely and artistically minted.
It can be melted to extract metal worth Rs. 10 out of it.
Its value is backed by the issuing authority.
Its intrinsic value is greater than Rs. 10.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** its value is backed by the issuing authority.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The **issuing authority,** which is the **government **in this case, guarantees the** value of the coin.**
 
• This means that the coin can be used as a **medium of exchange,** as people trust that it is worth the value printed on it.
 
• The **ten rupee coin** is not finely or artistically minted, nor does it have an intrinsic value greater than **Rs. 10.**
 
• Its value is purely **symbolic** and based on the trust that people have in the issuing authority.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term** "issuing authority"** refers to the entity that is responsible for **creating and distributing currency.**
 
• In India, this is the **Reserve Bank of India **(RBI), which is the **central bank** of the country.
 
• Finely and artistically minted coins may have **aesthetic value**, but this does not necessarily make them more valuable as currency.
 
• The value of a coin is determined by its **purchasing power, **which is based on the trust that people have in the currency and the stability of the economy.
 
• The **intrinsic value of a coin** is the value of the metal or materials used to make it.
 
• For example, a gold coin may have an **intrinsic value** based on the current market price of gold.
 
• However, most modern currency is not based on intrinsic value, but on the **trust and confidence** that people have in the issuing authority.

questions.question: Which of the following cities was built by Humayun at Delhi?

__
 
• **Humayun** built the city of **Dinpanah in Delhi** during his reign as the **Mughal emperor.**
 
• The city was built as a refuge for his family and court during times of **war and unrest.**
 
• Dinpanah was located near the older city of** Purana Qila** and was connected to it by a bridge over the **Yamuna River.**
 
• Today, the remains of Dinpanah can be seen in the form of **ruins and archaeological sites** in the area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Akbarabad **was built by **Humayun's son Akbar** after he became the Mughal emperor.

 
 
• During his lifetime, Akbar had renamed **Agra** as Akbarabad.
 
• But following the **demise of Akbar**, the name was once more changed to Agra.
 
 
 
• **Muhammadabad** is not a historically significant city and is not related to Humayun or the Mughal Empire.
 
• **Siri** was an ancient city in Delhi that was** destroyed by Timur** in the **14th century** and was not rebuilt by Humayun.
 
 
• Delhi gave rise to Siri as its **second city,** but it was never taken.

questions.question: The political Part of the Indian Constitution has been largely drawn from which Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**British Constitution.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The **political part** of the Indian Constitution has been largely drawn from the **British Constitution.**
 
• The Indian Constitution has borrowed the** parliamentary form of government, the rule of law, the bicameral legislature,** and the** office of the governor** from the British Constitution.
 
• However, the Indian Constitution has also made several modifications to the **British model** to suit the Indian context.
 
• For instance, India has a federal system of government with a strong center, while the UK has a **unitary system.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Irish Constitution** has influenced the Indian Constitution in terms of the **Directive Principles of State Policy.**

 
 
• The Indian Constitution has borrowed the idea of **social and economic justice** from the Irish Constitution. 
 
 
 
• The **Australian Constitution** has influenced the Indian Constitution in terms of the **concurrent list**, which allows both the center and the states to make laws on certain subjects.
 
• The** US Constitution** has influenced the Indian Constitution in terms of **fundamental rights**, which are similar to the** Bill of Rights** in the US Constitution.
 
 
• However, the Indian Constitution has also made several modifications to the **US model,** such as the inclusion of **socio-economic rights.**

questions.question: Which of these is true about the second phase of the green revolution?

options.text: It covered the period of the 1980s.
It was introduced in areas with irrigation facilities.
It covered the period of the 1960s and 1970s.
It was introduced in Punjab and Uttar Pradesh regions.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It covered the period of the 1980s.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 **Period: **The second phase of the Green Revolution was introduced in the 1980s.
 
 
• 
 **Second Phase: **The second phase did involve the introduction of new technologies in areas with irrigation facilities.
 
 
• 
 **Technological Introduction: **The Green Revolution was a period of increased agricultural productivity in the mid-20th century, largely due to the introduction of new technologies, such as high-yielding crop varieties, irrigation, and fertilizers.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** first phase **of the Green Revolution occurred in the **1960s and 1970s.**
 
• During this period, only certain states such as** Punjab, ****Haryana**, **Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu**, etc. were using** HYV seeds.**
 
• The **second phase** of the Green Revolution did involve the introduction of new technologies in areas with irrigation facilities.
 
• The Second Green Revolution refers to the shift in **agricultural production** that is generally accepted as being required to feed and support the planet's expanding population.
 
• These calls were prompted, among other things, by concerns about **peak oil and rising food commodity prices.**
 
• **Punjab and Uttar Pradesh **were two of the regions where the Green Revolution was first introduced in India.

questions.question: The Monetary Policy Committee maintained a hawkish stand on the interest rates. In this context, 'hawkish' stand means __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**interest rates were increased.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• A **hawkish **stand on interest rates means that the** central bank** or **monetary policy committee** is inclined towards raising interest rates in order to control inflation.
 
• This is usually done to prevent the economy from overheating due to** excessive borrowing and spending**, which can lead to inflation.
 
• In contrast, a **dovish stand** on interest rates means that the central bank is more likely to** lower interest rates** to stimulate economic growth and borrowing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term **"hawkish"** comes from the idea of a** hawk,** which is known for being **aggressive and vigilant.**
 
• A hawkish monetary policy is characterized by a more **aggressive stance** toward controlling inflation and maintaining price stability.
 
• In contrast, a **"dovish" monetary policy **is named after the image of a dove, which is associated with **peace and tranquility.**
 
• A dovish policy is more focused on stimulating **economic growth and reducing unemployment**, even if it means accepting a higher level of inflation.

questions.question: Which are the four quantum numbers for an electron present in 4f orbital?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** n = 4, I = 3, m = +1, s = +1/2.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **four quantum numbers** for an electron present in **4f orbital **are **n = 4, l = 3, m = +1, and s = +1/2.**
 
• The **principal quantum number (n)** indicates the** energy level **of the electron, and for 4f orbital, it is 4.
 
• The **azimuthal quantum number** (l) determines the **shape of the orbital**, and for f orbital, it can have values from** 0 to n-1**, which gives l = 3.
 
• The **magnetic quantum number** (m) specifies the **orientation of the orbital** in space and can have values from **-l to +l**, which gives m = +1 for the 4f orbital.
 
• The **spin quantum number** (s) describes the intrinsic angular momentum of the electron and can have two values, **+1/2 or -1/2**, for the electron in 4f orbital, it is +1/2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quantum Numbers** are a set of numbers that describe the** properties** of an electron in an atom, including its **energy level, orbital shape, orientation, and spin.**
 
• The characteristics of **atomic orbitals **and the electrons within them are described by quantum numbers.
 
• There are **four quantum numbers** that represent the states of an electron in an atom or an ion.

questions.question: What is the product of the reaction when anhydrite undergoes hydration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gypsum.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anhydrite** is a mineral that has the chemical formula** CaSO₄.**
 
• It is an** anhydrous form** of gypsum.
 
• When anhydrite undergoes **hydration**, it reacts with water to form gypsum (CaSO₄.2H₂O).
 
• Therefore, the product of the reaction when **anhydrite undergoes** hydration is gypsum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gypsum **is a **soft sulfate mineral** that is widely used in construction as a building material.

 
 
• It is also used in **agriculture, medicine, and other industries.**
 
 
 
• **Limonite** is a type of** iron ore** that is **brownish-yellow** in color.
 
 
• It can precipitate from surface or groundwater that is rich in iron, and it forms from the **weathering **of other iron minerals.
 
 
 
• **Magnesite** is a mineral that has the chemical formula **MgCO₃**.
 
 
• The mineral was created either by the action of magnesium-containing solutions on** calcite **or as an alteration product from rocks rich in magnesium.
 
 
 
• **Kaolin** is a type of clay mineral that is used in **ceramics, paper,** and other industries.
 
 
• The fine particle size, plate-like or **lamellar particle shape**, and chemical inertness of hydrous kaolin are its distinguishing features.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is transmitted by the bite of an infected phlebotomine sandfly, characterised by irregular fever, weight loss and enlargement of the spleen and liver?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Visceral leishmaniasis.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Visceral leishmaniasis**, also known as **kala-azar**, is a parasitic disease caused by the **Leishmania donovani parasite,** which is transmitted by the bite of an** infected phlebotomine sandfly.**
 
• The disease is characterized by **irregular fever, weight loss,** and **enlargement of the spleen and liver**, which can lead to** serious health complications** if left untreated.
 
• Treatment for visceral leishmaniasis typically involves a combination of drugs such as** liposomal amphotericin B, miltefosine, and paromomycin.**
 
• Prevention measures for the disease include using **insect repellent**, wearing **protective clothing**, and sleeping under **insecticide-treated bed nets.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Japanese encephalitis** is a viral disease transmitted by** mosquitoes.**

 
 
• It can cause **inflammation of the brain** and is endemic in parts of Asia.
 
 
 
• **Diarrhea** is a common condition characterized by **loose or watery stools.**
 
 
• It can be caused by a variety of factors such as **infections, food intolerances, and medications.**
 
 
 
• **Anaplasmosis** is a tick-borne disease caused by the **Anaplasma phagocytophilum bacterium**.
 
 
• It can cause **fever, headache, and muscle aches.**

questions.question: In which year was the Indian National Congress established?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1885.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1885** is the year in which a group of prominent Indian leaders, including **Allan Octavian Hume** and **Dadabhai Naoroji**, founded the Congress.
 
• It was founded with the goal of advocating for** Indian independence **from **British rule** and promoting Indian interests. 
 
• Over the years, the Congress has played a significant role in India's struggle for** independence** and in shaping the country's political landscape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• INC was the first contemporary **nationalist movement** to arise in Asia and Africa under the British Empire.
 
• Congress, which came into being as a** secular,** all-encompassing party following** India's independence in 1947,** dominated Indian politics for the next twenty years.
 
• **Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru,** the party's first prime minister, convinced the Congress to back socialist policies by instituting a mixed economy, forming a **secular state,** forming the** Planning Commission**, and introducing **Five-Year Plans.**
 
• Following the demise of Nehru and the brief administration of** Lal Bahadur Shastri, Indira Gandhi **assumed the role of party leader.

questions.question: According to the Indian Minerals Yearbook 2020, which state has the highest production of manganese in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Madhya Pradesh** has the highest production of manganese in India, with a production of** 5,528 thousand tonnes** in the year 2019-20, according to the Indian Minerals Yearbook 2020.
 
• Manganese is an important mineral used in the production of **steel and other alloys.**
 
• India is the** fifth-largest producer **of manganese in the world.
 
• Madhya Pradesh has several manganese mines, including the **Balaghat mine**, which is one of the largest manganese mines in Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Karnataka** is the **second-highest producer** of manganese in India with a production of **4,961 thousand tonnes** in 2019-20.
 
• **Odisha** is the** third highest **producer of manganese in India with a production of **3,808 thousand tonnes** in** 2019-20**.
 
• **Maharashtra** produced **1,271 thousand tonnes **of manganese in 2019-20, which is** lower** than the top three manganese-producing states.
 
• **Manganese **is mainly used in the production of **steel, aluminum, and batteries.**
 
• It is also used in the production of** fertilizers, animal feed, and water treatment chemicals.**

questions.question: Article 22 of the Indian Constitution is related to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Preventive detention.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 22** of the Indian Constitution deals with the** right to protection** against** arrest and detention** in certain cases. 
 
• It lays down the guidelines for preventive detention, which means **detaining a person without trial** for a certain period, in order to prevent him/her from committing a crime.
 
• This article also ensures that a person who is arrested has the right to be informed about the **grounds of arrest,** and the right to consult and be defended by a **legal practitioner **of his/her choice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The right to education** is covered under** Article 21A** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Protection of personal liberty** is covered under **Article 21** of the Indian Constitution, while Article 22 deals with protection against **arrest and detention **in certain cases.
 
• **Protection of life** is covered under **Article 21 **of the Indian Constitution, while Article 22 deals with protection against **arrest and detention **in certain cases.

questions.question: Which of the following industries is its own major consumer in India?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The** chemical industry** is its own** major consumer **in India as it produces a wide range of products that are used in various sectors such as **agriculture, textiles, pharmaceuticals, and construction.**
 
• The chemical industry is one of the oldest industries in India and is a significant contributor to the country's economy, accounting for around** 2% of India's GDP.**
 
• The key term mentioned in the question is "**its own major consumer,**" which means the industry that** produces products** that are primarily used within the same industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The iron and steel industry** is one of the** largest industries** in India and is a major contributor to the country's economy.
 
• It is used in various sectors such as **construction, infrastructure, and automobile.**
 
• **The aviation industry** in India is growing rapidly, and it plays a crucial role in connecting various parts of the** country and promoting tourism.** 
 
• **The automobile industry** is also one of the **largest industries in India **and is a significant contributor to the country's economy.
 
• It is used in various sectors such as **transportation, logistics, and construction**.
